findings.route: hard-stop — do not patch; fold into the declared ceiling
findings.claim: The new line-continuation join creates a fresh default-GREEN hole that did not exist before this repair: a comment line ending in a backslash swallows the following COPY instruction, so `COPY . /app/` becomes invisible to the guard.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py `text = re.sub(r"\\\n[ \t]*", " ", text)`. Docker strips comment lines BEFORE continuation handling, so in `# x \<newline>COPY . /app/` the COPY is a real instruction Docker executes. The join rewrites it to `# x  COPY . /app/` and the parser returns []. Regression, not pre-existing: the retired regex returns ['COPY . /app/'] on the same input.
findings.repro: Orchestrator-verified: `_dockerfile_copies('# x \\\nCOPY . /app/\n')` -> `[]`; end-to-end with that substitution -> `passed=True, wrong={}` while the whole context including `.git` ships.
findings.acceptance: Under the hard stop this is NOT patched. It is named verbatim in ADR-034's declared ceiling and in the debt block as a third demonstrated evasion class (after instruction spelling and `RUN --mount`), as evidence that text-parsing a Dockerfile cannot carry the guarantee.

findings.route: repair — prose mandatory, one-character regex fix recommended
findings.claim: The diff's own enumeration of which regexes remain case-sensitive is wrong in the dangerous direction: the `ARG ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` conjunct is case-sensitive and fails OPEN, not closed.
findings.evidence: Case JSON ceiling (4) states the remaining case-sensitive regexes 'fail CLOSED ... Loud and wrong, never quiet and wrong', omitting `re.findall(r"(?m)^\s*ARG\s+ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA.*$", text)`. `arg ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` is valid Docker and passes, so the supplied-sha channel the conjunct exists to forbid can be reintroduced with the check green.
findings.repro: Orchestrator-verified: lowercase `arg ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` -> `passed=True, wrong={}`; uppercase control -> `['build_arg_still_declared']`.
findings.acceptance: Ceiling (4) names ARG explicitly as case-sensitive and failing OPEN, and retracts 'never quiet and wrong'. Applying `(?i)` to that one regex is recommended — it is the case-insensitivity fix R10 already established applied to a regex that was missed, not a new spelling chase — but the prose correction is required either way.

findings.claim: Four documents added by this diff claim a lowercase `FROM` was probed and 'fails closed / reports single_stage / is red'; lowercasing the derive stage's FROM in fact raises an uncaught ValueError inside the check, so the stated conjunct is never reported.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py `stage_i = max(i for i, s in enumerate(stages) if s.start() <= derive.start())` raises `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty` when the first FROM is lowercased. Claims falsified in: the case JSON ceiling (4), ADR-034 ('all three fail closed, loudly'), tasks/TODO.md, and tasks/reviews/pr67-r3-resolution.json (`fail_closed_neighbours` 'all three are red'). Lowercasing only the FINAL stage's FROM does report `single_stage` — the derive-stage spelling was evidently not the one probed.
findings.repro: Orchestrator-verified: shipped Dockerfile with the first `FROM mcr` -> `from mcr` yields `ValueError('max() iterable argument is empty')`, not `single_stage`.
findings.acceptance: Either the check guards the empty-stage case so a lowercase derive-stage FROM reports a named conjunct, or all four documents are corrected to say what actually happens and to name the spelling that WAS probed. A document asserting a verification that did not happen is the failure this repo exists to prevent.
